reasoning_summary: 0001 ("The problem is false as stated"): legitimate thesis statement; the asker explicitly invites refutation, and nothing is assumed yet. OK as a claim to be supported. 0002: blank. 0003 ("Let a be any integer such that a^{p-1} = 1 mod p^2"): justified setup; this is exactly the n=2 instance of the hypothesis, and it forces gcd(a,p)=1, so the class is nonempty and admissible. OK. 0004: display delimiter. 0005 (factorization display): the intended identity is a^{p(p-1)} - 1 = (a^{p-1}-1)((a^{p-1})^{p-1} + ... + (a^{p-1})^1 + 1), i.e. x^p - 1 = (x-1)(x^{p-1}+...+x+1) with x = a^{p-1}; the RHS sum has exactly the p terms i=0..p-1, so the identity is correct. The LHS is typeset as "a^{p(p-1)-1}" instead of "a^{p(p-1)} - 1", an obvious typesetting slip that the very next step reads correctly; not a mathematical failure. OK. 0006: display delimiter. 0007 (divisibility conclusion): correct — p^2 | a^{p-1}-1 by assumption; each of the p summands (a^{p-1})^i = 1 mod p^2, so the second factor = p mod p^2 and is divisible by p (exactly once); hence p^2 * p = p^3 divides a^{p(p-1)} - 1, i.e. a^{p(p-1)} = 1 mod p^3. Justified. 0008: blank. 0009 ("Similarly"): correct signposting of the iterated step. OK. 0010: display delimiter. 0011 (second factorization): same identity with x = a^{p(p-1)}; correct as written (again modulo the same LHS typeset slip). OK. 0012: display delimiter. 0013 (induction claim): justified — base case n=2 is the hypothesis a^{p-1} = 1 mod p^2; if a^{p^{n-2}(p-1)} = 1 mod p^n then the factorization gives p^n from the first factor and p from the second factor (which is = p mod p^n since n >= 2), so p^{n+1} | a^{p^{n-1}(p-1)} - 1. So the whole infinite family of congruences is equivalent to the single n=2 congruence, which is the correct diagnosis of the asker's error. OK. 0014: blank. 0015 (concrete counterexamples): FIRST FAILING STEP. The general assertions here are fine and the numerical checks (7,5) and (17,3) are correct: 7^4 = 2401 = 1 mod 25 and 17^2 = 289 = 1 mod 9, and neither 7 nor 17 is a p-th power; likewise a^{p-1} mod p^2 depends only on a mod p^2, so adding p^2 preserves the congruence. But the step then asserts that "(32,5) and (57,5) and (82,5) ... are all counterexamples as well", and 32 = 2^5 IS a perfect 5th power (z = 2), so (32,5) satisfies the hypothesis and the conclusion a = z^p and is therefore not a counterexample at all. Since the step's declared job is to supply composite counterexamples (the original claim restricts to composite a, so 7 and 17 do not by themselves refute it), the first composite instance offered is false, and the step as written is not justified. Note the defect is local and repairable: 57 = 3*19 and 82 = 2*41 are both = 7 mod 25, coprime to 5, composite, and not 5th powers, so genuine composite counterexamples do exist and the overall refutation of the claim survives; but step 0015 as stated contains a false assertion.
